archetypes.name: reader-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan relocates three Codex-written artifacts but explicitly names only step-7a.sh as a reader; any other script that reads manifest.json, qa-pending.json, or codex-impl-transcript.txt from the IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR root would silently break after the move.
archetypes.prompt_body: Search every script under skills/, scripts/, and .claude/ for references that read codex-impl-transcript.txt, manifest.json, or qa-pending.json from the session tmpdir root using patterns like $IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR/manifest.json, $IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR/qa-pending.json, or $IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR/codex-impl-transcript. Compare every hit against the plan's stated affected-files list (step-7a.sh, step2-implement.sh, launch-codex-implement.sh, test-codex-implementer.sh, test-step2-dispatch.sh) and flag any script that reads from the tmpdir root but is absent from that list. Also check whether manifest-raw.json — explicitly kept at the root in the plan — is referenced anywhere in a way that could be confused with the relocated manifest.json (e.g. by glob or partial-path match). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: session-tmpdir-derivation
archetypes.rationale: The plan's entire auto-narrowing mechanism depends on SESSION_TMPDIR being derived from dirname(MANIFEST_PATH) inside launch-codex-implement.sh; if the launcher sets SESSION_TMPDIR from IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR or another fixed env var, moving MANIFEST_PATH into a subdir does not narrow the --add-dir grant at all.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read scripts/launch-codex-implement.sh and locate every assignment to SESSION_TMPDIR (or the variable that feeds --add-dir). Verify whether it is actually computed as dirname of the --manifest-path argument at the point where --add-dir is constructed, or whether it is assigned from IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR, an env var, or any other source that would not change when MANIFEST_PATH moves into a subdir. If SESSION_TMPDIR is not derived from MANIFEST_PATH, the plan's central auto-narrowing premise is false and explicit --add-dir changes would be required instead. Also confirm that the new TRANSCRIPT_PARENT parity check is placed after SESSION_TMPDIR is established so the error-exit path is reachable, and that the check fires before the Codex spawn rather than after. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-table-coverage
archetypes.rationale: The plan lists 16 specific test IDs in test-step2-dispatch.sh requiring STEP2_MANIFEST_PATH updates, but any codex-path test omitted from the table would still write to the old tmpdir root and produce a silent manifest-missing failure in CI.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read skills/implement/scripts/test-step2-dispatch.sh and enumerate every test block that sets STEP2_MANIFEST_PATH, STUB_MANIFEST_PATH, or an equivalent path variable for a codex stub invocation, then cross-check each one against the plan's table (12a, 12b, 13, 16, 17a, 17b, 17c, 18, M1, M2, M12, M16, M17, M18-both-invocations, M19, 25) and flag any codex-path test not listed. Read skills/implement/scripts/test-codex-implementer.sh and verify that the update scope (tests 4–7+ plus the new 11c) covers every test that hard-codes a manifest, qa-pending, or transcript path at SCRATCH or IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR_FIXTURE root rather than in a subdir. For test-codex-implementer.sh specifically, the plan says to manually create codex-step2-out/ in the test setup — confirm whether tests that call the launcher directly (bypassing step2-implement.sh) would otherwise find that subdir absent, since step2-implement.sh's mkdir -p would not have run. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
